invention_title: Damage Rate Deceleration as a Pre-Fragmentation Signal in Thrombectomy
invention_description: A method for predicting material fragmentation during mechanical thrombectomy by monitoring the rate of change of the continuum damage variable (dD/dstrain). When the damage rate decelerates (transitions from accelerating to decelerating growth), fragmentation onset is predicted before the damage variable D reaches its critical threshold D_critical. The method provides advance warning of clot fragmentation, enabling the surgeon to adjust retrieval parameters before embolic fragment generation.

technical_claim.mechanism: Continuum damage mechanics (CDM) with Simo cumulative distribution function
technical_claim.signal: Deceleration of dD/dstrain (the damage growth rate slows before fracture)
technical_claim.prediction: Fragmentation occurs when D crosses D_critical=0.9. The dD/dstrain peak (deceleration onset) occurs BEFORE D reaches D_critical, providing a lead time of 0.02-18.0 strain (mean 2.5 strain).
technical_claim.detection_method: Monitor D trajectory during retrieval. Compute dD/dstrain in real time. Signal fires when dD/dstrain transitions from increasing to decreasing (peak detected).
technical_claim.action_on_signal: Reduce retrieval force or pause retrieval to prevent fragmentation
advantage_over_alternatives: D absolute threshold (D > 0.85): simpler but LATER warning — dD/dstrain deceleration provides earlier prediction
Stress monitoring: stress is an indirect indicator; D is the direct damage variable
Acoustic emission: requires additional hardware; dD/dstrain can be computed from force/displacement sensors

validity_domain.constraint: D_max = 1 - beta > D_critical = 0.9 (i.e., beta < 0.1 for fracture to occur)
validity_domain.exclusions: beta >= 0.10 (no fracture occurs, D saturates below D_critical)
